metadata.title: Why Giving an AI Agent More Tools Can Make It Worse — Build a Progressive Tool Router with Claude
alternative_titles: 1,000 AI Tools vs. 3 — Why More Context Can Make an Agent Worse
Build a Smart MCP Tool Router with Claude: Load Only the Tools Your AI Needs
metadata.central_question: If an AI agent has access to 1,000 tools, should all 1,000 be placed in its context?
metadata.answer: No — read the intent, retrieve and rank candidate tools, load only the top few.

metadata.claim_policy: No measured token/latency/cost/accuracy numbers until the benchmark (blueprint section E) is run. Illustrative values must carry an on-screen ILLUSTRATIVE EXAMPLE plate for their full life. Never claim that more tools make a model less intelligent.

beats.narration: Hi, I am Dhrumil Shah, and this video is about why giving an AI agent more tools can actually make it worse — and how we can build a smarter progressive tool router with Claude.
beats.visual: Terminal caret types the name; terracotta underline sweeps; five ghosted pipeline chips preview the film.

beats.narration: If an AI agent has access to a thousand tools, does it really need all thousand in its context just to analyze one CSV file?
beats.visual: 1,000-dot tool cloud (25x40) pulses left; single CSV glyph right; large terracotta question mark snaps in on the word really.

beats.narration: Every tool costs context before the work even starts — a name, a description, an input schema, parameters, permissions.
beats.visual: Tool card expands into five metadata rows, each highlighting on its spoken word; context bar starts filling in the definitions colour.

beats.narration: Multiply that by a thousand and the context fills with menu instead of meal — bigger search space, more latency, more cost, more chances to pick the wrong tool.
beats.visual: Seven-link vertical chain builds with down-arrows; final link flashes amber with a warning glyph.

beats.narration: Take a real request: analyze this CSV and create a chart. The agent loads a thousand definitions, searches them all, and ends up using three.
on_screen_text: USER: Analyze this CSV and create a chart.
beats.visual: Dot cloud flows into the agent node; magnifier sweeps; exactly three dots light teal and rise as named chips while 997 stay grey.

beats.narration: Progressive discovery flips it. Read the intent first, search a tool registry, and load only what the task needs.
beats.visual: Four-stage vertical flow lights in order; 997 irrelevant dots dissolve downward; the three chips continue into the agent.

beats.narration: Claude can help you build each piece: intent classification, a tool registry, semantic search, ranking, top-K selection, then execution.
beats.visual: Eight-stage stack builds in sync with narration; a data pulse travels the completed chain.

beats.narration: The code stays small: search the registry, rank against the query, keep the top three, and hand those to Claude.
on_screen_text: query = analyze this CSV and create a chart
beats.visual: Code types line by line on a dark card; on [:3] three chips snap in and a counter ticks 1,000 to 3.

beats.narration: Same thousand tools. Method A exposes a thousand. Method B exposes three. Same job, far less overhead.
on_screen_text: exposed 1,000 · relevant 3 · context overhead HIGH · routing complexity HIGH
exposed 3 · relevant 3 · context overhead LOW · routing complexity LOWER
beats.visual: Two stacked cards with vertically aligned rows; ILLUSTRATIVE EXAMPLE plate visible for the whole scene.

beats.narration: This is information retrieval, ranking algorithms, software architecture, distributed systems and context engineering, in one build.
beats.visual: Six chips land in a 2x3 grid, each with a small glyph.

beats.narration: This matters as ecosystems grow. Anthropic's tool search tool already defers loading until Claude needs a tool, and the MCP roadmap calls progressive discovery a priority — check the official docs before you quote any specifics.
on_screen_text: CURRENT-DEVELOPMENT INFO — VERIFY AGAINST OFFICIAL DOCS
beats.visual: Three MCP server nodes connect to one client; only matched tool chips travel the wire into the agent.
Five words light one per spoken word, then compress into a rotating ring.

beats.narration: The goal isn't to give an AI agent every tool at once. The goal is to give it the right tools at the right time.
on_screen_text: THE RIGHT TOOLS AT THE RIGHT TIME
beats.visual: First line greys and strikes through; second line scales up in terracotta; background dims to isolate the type.

beats.narration: Progressive tool discovery can make agent systems more focused, efficient and easier to scale. I'm Dhrumil Shah, and this is how smarter tool routing helps us build better AI agents.
beats.visual: Pipeline redraws as a ribbon, then the end card settles with title, presenter and repo folder.
